notes.hook: The bold claim and text overlay immediately grab attention by challenging our perception of the solar system.
notes.clarity: The middle section loses the narrative thread by pivoting to general Jupiter trivia instead of explaining the shrinkage.
notes.payoff: There is no explanation of why it was larger or why it shrunk, leaving the hook's curiosity unsatisfied.
notes.visuals: The use of an exoplanet (51 Eri b) and overly complex, text-heavy charts makes the video look unprofessional.
notes.loop: The repetition of the 'twice as wide' line makes for a perfectly seamless transition.

frames.problem: mostly text and too small to read on a phone
subject is too small with multiple instances making it look cluttered
wrong object; image shows exoplanet 51 Eri b instead of Jupiter

rewrite: Beat 5: Even after shrinking, its gravity remains terrifying.
Beat 6: It rotates so fast that days last only ten hours.
Beat 7: Stretching its moons and feeding storms larger than Earth.
rounds.better_than_last: This Short provides a perfectly seamless vocal and visual loop that is much more effective than the ending of Episode 414.

notes.hook: A clear, massive scale-based hook that immediately recontextualizes a familiar planet.
notes.clarity: Logical progression from ancient size to current power and rotation.
notes.payoff: The contrast between its current dominance and its former ghost self is satisfying.
notes.visuals: Beat 5 is very blurry and pixelated, and technical diagrams in 3 and 6 are hard to read on mobile.
notes.loop: Perfectly seamless transition that repeats the core hook phrase.

frames.problem: Technical diagram with small, cropped text is illegible at phone size.
Visual is extremely blurry and pixelated, appearing like a low-resolution error.
Grid of twelve images with tiny captions is too busy and small for a vertical Short.

rounds.better_than_last: The use of comparative scale (8,000 Earths) creates a much stronger mental image than the technical details in ep413.

notes.hook: The concrete comparison of Jupiter being twice its current width is a strong, immediate attention-grabber.
notes.clarity: The narrative flow from ancient scale to current orbital and atmospheric dominance is very easy to follow.
notes.payoff: The closing realization that the modern giant is just a ghost of its former self is a satisfying thematic wrap-up.
notes.visuals: The use of an exoplanet chart in beat 3 and a very blurry render in beat 5 are significant quality issues.
notes.loop: The final line mirrors the opening premise perfectly, making the replay transition completely seamless.

frames.problem: The image shows the Kepler-51 exoplanet system instead of the solar system planets mentioned in the script.
The frame is a blurry, abstract red mass that fails to clearly represent the planet or the concept of gravity.

rounds.better_than_last: This Short achieves a much more seamless verbal loop than the recent 'Ghost Module' or 'Biggest Thing in Space' episodes.
